content.comment_body: We want to transfer our updated program to the [product_name] ([article_no]) using a portable PC on the workfloor. We use [product_name] [product_name] [version_no]. Our portable PC does not have a standard RS232 serial port, so we purchased a PCMCIA card to add RS232 connectivity. The card creates a COM4 port, but when we try to send the program, we receive an error saying "You must use the newest software." We also installed the latest update from [company_name]'s website, but transfer still fails. Using a regular PC with a built-in RS232 port works without issues, but bringing a full desktop PC onto the workfloor is not ideal. We would appreciate any advice.

It appears your PCMCIA card does not properly emulate a serial port for use with [product_name]. Since your PC lacks an integrated serial port, the best alternative is to use a USB/serial converter. Online, there are two USB/serial converters known to work reliably with [product_name], though many others are available—compatibility is not guaranteed for all devices. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulties transferring programs to [product_name] using a portable PC with a PCMCIA RS232 card and [product_name] [version_no]. The software reported it was outdated despite updates. Transfers succeeded with a desktop PC's built-in RS232 port, underscoring compatibility issues when using adapters and portable setups.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expected smooth program transfers using portable PCs equipped with third-party serial adapters and up-to-date software, assuming that upgrading to the latest software would resolve communication problems.
